svg.title: Figure 2: cost curves X, Y, Z and the AR = MR line
svg.desc: A graph with the vertical axis labelled 'Cost/Revenue' and the horizontal axis labelled 'Output/Sales', origin marked O. A horizontal line at a height marked P runs across the graph and is labelled 'AR = MR' where it meets the right edge. Three curves, each dipping down from the left and then curving back up to the right, are labelled X, Y and Z. Curve X sits above the others on the left, dips to its lowest point, then rises very steeply on the right, crossing above line P and ending as the highest of the three curves at the top right. Curve Y dips to its lowest point a little further right than X, then rises more gently than X, crossing line P further to the right, and ends below X at the top right. Curve Z lies below both X and Y for most of the graph, dips to its lowest point furthest to the right, and rises most gently of the three, staying closest to line P and crossing it last, furthest to the right. Four dashed vertical lines run from the horizontal axis up into the curves, marked from left to right R, Q, S and T.
